name: PT Temas Tbk.

frontmatter.title: Temas: a second index flow on a container fleet that earns
frontmatter.summary: FTSE Russell deletes the HSC-category names, Temas among them, from its global indices at the open on 21 December 2026 - a passive sale the konglo lens does not charge, on top of the exchange's HSC exclusion. The container business is unchanged: the lens still targets Rp127 against Rp113, a 16.7% total return, and we keep the ADD.
thesis: The deletion is a second flow, not the same fact twice: FTSE Russell removes the Indonesian names in the HSC category from its global indices at the open on 21 December 2026 and Temas is one of them, an uncharged passive sale on top of the domestic index exclusion, and no volume, rate, cost or fleet input in our model changes [S19][S10].
Earnings power is under-priced: nine-month profit already exceeded the whole of the prior year, yet the shares trade at 6.8x of our FY2026E earnings and 5.6x of corrected EBITDA.
The margin is not only a rate spike: capacity 17% larger met revenue growth of 37% with cost of services up 23%, which is load factor and vertical integration working together [S4][S8].
Capex falls from 45.2% of revenue to 12.0% by the end of the forecast, releasing the cash the fleet was bought with [S8].
The float is 14.83% against the 15% minimum due by 31 March 2027; we value Rp138 fundamentally and target Rp127 after the lens, a 16.7% return [S14][S17].

catalysts.event: Quarterly HSC committee review; changes take effect two sessions after the announcement
FTSE Russell revision window closes; the deletion list can still change
FTSE Russell sets the final December review list
Deletion from the FTSE Russell global indices takes effect at the open
Deadline for the {{fact.F25|num0}}% minimum free float
FY2026 audited accounts due, the first full year on the enlarged fleet
MSCI consultation on Standalone status: market-participant feedback closes
MSCI announces its decision on reclassifying Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone

blocks.text: What changed is the shareholder base, not the business. FTSE Russell's December 2026 quarterly review removes the Indonesian names in the HSC category from its global indices, effective at the open on 21 December 2026, and Temas is one of the nine micro-caps on the list [S19]. The revision window closes on 4 December and the final list is set on 7 December [S18]. No operating input moves, and the engine still gives a fundamental value of Rp138 twelve months out against a price of Rp113: a target of Rp127 and a 16.7% total return [S0][S8].

For the twelve-month most-likely price the deletion is a path, not a level. Index-tracking money must sell at the effective date whatever the container market is doing, so the shares carry a mechanical supply event inside our window; no source gives the index weight or the passive assets tracking it, and we will not invent an outflow [S19]. It is a second flow rather than a second charge for the first: the lens prices the HSC status that took the shares out of the IHSG calculation on 13 November 2026 and out of the LQ45, IDX30, IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [S10], and FTSE Russell's deletion of the 14 HSC-category names lands on top of that [S19]. The base regime closes only 20.0% of the log gap and leaves the rest open, which is what a dated passive sale into a 14.83% float implies [S10][S19]. For the ADD, a flow-driven fall while the fleet keeps earning widens the discount, holds the target and raises the expected return; we size the position for a December drawdown rather than change the rating.

The case is the one we published. Nine-month net profit already exceeded the whole of FY2025, with capacity 17% larger meeting revenue growth of 37% and cost of services up only 23% [S4][S12]. The shares trade at 6.8x of FY2026E earnings and 5.6x of corrected EBITDA, while capex steps down to 12.0% of revenue by the end of the forecast [S0][S8]. Two things move the value: the durability of the gross margin, where every point held is worth more than a point of revenue growth, and the form of the free-float fix due by 31 March 2027 - a sell-down that improves the tape or new shares that cost the minority little at this gap [S4][S17].

Temas is a vertically integrated container logistics group built around three activities that share one cargo flow. PT Temas Shipping operates the line: 57 vessels with 28,542 TEU across more than 60 ports, on regular, project and sea-toll routes [S6][S8]. PT Temas Port handles stevedoring, equipment rental and trucking at the berths the group operates, and PT Temas Depot runs 10 container depots in Jakarta, Surabaya, Makassar, Bitung and Belawan [S6]. The accounts report two segments; shipping is 96% of consolidated revenue [S16].

Integration is the business model: a line owning its berth slots and depots captures the stevedoring margin a pure carrier leaves with the terminal operator, and management's stated strategy is fleet modernisation and route optimisation [S5][S6]. The company added vessels net in 2025 and cut average vessel age from fifteen years in 2023 to 13 years [S8]. The 2026 capital budget is IDR2,500.0bn, and by September IDR917.2bn of vessel down payments had been paid [S8][S4]. Alongside sit a build-operate-transfer arrangement with Pelindo Terminal Petikemas to extend the Tanjung Priok berth and an LNG plant due in the second half of 2026 [S8].

Ownership is concentrated. PT Temas Lestari holds 83.66%, the public 15.56% in stakes each below five per cent, with treasury shares the small balance, and the IDX-IC registry puts the free float at 14.83% [S14][S16]. The HSC screen counts the top ten holders, including nominee accounts inside the public float, so a top-ten total at or above 92.5% is consistent with a public stake of 15.56% [S10][S16].

The industry is the domestic leg of Indonesian container logistics. Pelindo Terminal Petikemas moved 13.34 million TEU in 2025, up 6.87% on 2024, with the international segment growing on exports to the United States and China [S9]: high single-digit growth in boxes, plus whatever share the private lines take from each other.

Temas sits in the private, integrated end of that market. Its 57 ships and 28,542 TEU make it one of the larger domestic operators, and the 60 ports it calls at give it national reach [S8][S6]. The competitive set is a handful of Indonesian-owned lines plus Pelindo at the terminal layer, which is also Temas's BOT partner at Tanjung Priok - a relationship that matters more than any single competitor, because berth access is the binding constraint [S8].

On the five forces the picture is mixed but favourable to an incumbent. Supplier power is rising, because bunker fuel is dollar-priced and second-hand vessel prices set the entry cost of capacity [S8]. Buyer power is moderate: switching a shipment is cheap, switching a contracted network is not [S6]. New entry is constrained by capital and berth slots; substitutes are toll roads, ro-ro and air freight [S8]. Rivalry runs on reliability and coverage rather than price [S6]. The house macro deck has the rupiah at 18,350 against the dollar in FY2027E, a headwind arriving with a lag for a company that buys fuel and leases tonnage in dollars [S0]. Regulation cuts both ways: sea-toll lanes are underwritten, while the free-float and HSC rules govern how the equity trades [S17][S10].

The moat is distribution density: a national port network a challenger would have to replicate berth by berth, widening slowly through the Priok extension and the depots [S6][S8]. It is not a network effect, so margin fades toward the cost of capital rather than crediting a perpetual excess return.

The record is a flat revenue line and a compressing margin, then a step change: revenue stayed in a narrow band from IDR4.88tn in FY2022 to IDR4.35tn in FY2025, while gross profit fell from IDR1.77tn to IDR0.80tn and the margin from 36.2% to 18.3%; net profit fell to IDR499.2bn on a cost of services rise of 3.20% against flat revenue [S0][S12].

FY2026 broke the pattern, and the filing gives nine-month totals, not a quarterly sequence. Nine-month revenue reached IDR4,380.0bn against IDR4.35tn for the whole of the prior year, cost of services rose 23% rather than in line, and gross profit roughly doubled to IDR1,140.0bn [S4]. The mechanism is operating leverage on a fixed fleet: capacity rose 17% in 2025 and revenue is up 37% in nine months, so the residual is rate and utilisation inside the shipping line, not a new business [S16]. Our FY2026E revenue of IDR5,540.7bn is the nine-month actual plus a flat Q4 and matches the company's IDR5,530.0bn target [S4][S8][S15].

We model a gross margin of 26.0% for FY2026E, fading to 23.2% by FY2030E and 22.5% at the end of the forecast [S4][S12]. The fade is the most contestable assumption: the 2026 level is a multi-year high driven by a firm freight market, and the dollar cost base does not fall when the rupiah weakens [S0]. SG&A stays at 4.0% of revenue, close to the FY2025 actual, because it is largely fixed [S0].

The fourth quarter is where a flat carry has to be defended, and we state it: FY2026E holds the nine-month rate on a flat Q4, which is not a bet on a stronger year-end. In 2025 the fourth quarter printed *above* its own nine-month rate — nine-month revenue of IDR3,190.0bn against nine-month gross profit of IDR567.8bn, and a full year of IDR4,348.4bn against IDR797.5bn [S4][S12]. Carrying the 2026 nine-month rate into Q4 therefore assumes no further improvement on a year that has run well above cost growth, and Q4 2026 carries a full quarter of the enlarged fleet that was not there a year earlier [S8]. The seasonal-reversion case is the bear scenario, not the base.

The pack's depreciation line is not usable: IDR398.7bn against IDR4,196.4bn of net PP&E, because the filings use the direct method and the pack captures only a residual [S0]. From the audited fixed-asset note total depreciation was IDR398.7bn in FY2025A and IDR418.5bn in FY2024A, rebuilding FY2025A EBITDA at IDR1,125.2bn and a 25.9% margin [S16]. We model 7.6% of revenue, the nine-month run-rate with a Q4 charge on the new ships [S15].

Cash conversion has been good for two audited years running: operating cash flow of IDR829.2bn covered net profit of IDR499.2bn in FY2025A, and IDR992.3bn covered IDR673.4bn in FY2024A, so accruals run negative in both years on total assets of IDR5,291.0bn and IDR4,409.5bn [S16]. One flag: receivables rose from IDR258.6bn to IDR306.3bn, roughly a fifth, on flat revenue, which is a divergence [S16]. Related-party revenue is only 0.29% of the total, so this is not related-party gravity; it is a voyage-completion timing issue we cannot explain at note level, and we class it optics rather than clean [S16].

Capex was IDR1,089.0bn in FY2024 and IDR1,402.9bn in FY2025, the 2026 budget is IDR2,500.0bn, and long-term loans drew IDR929.2bn in nine months [S0][S8][S4]. We carry net new borrowing of about the whole funding gap, taking gross debt to IDR2,666.5bn and leaving cash of IDR44.0bn; net debt to EBITDA reaches 1.6x and falls as capex steps down to 12.0% of revenue [S4][S0]. The fleet is bought and the depreciation is non-cash.

The dividend policy is a 30% payout once profit passes a disclosed threshold, and FY2025 was paid at 40%, 4 rupiah a share [S2]. We model the policy rate, not the bumper year; there is no buyback or rights issue in the plan [S0][S8].
Earnings-quality gate. The house screen, run on the audited FY2025 accounts and the registry [S16]:

| Screen | Evidence | Read | Class | |---|---|---|---| | Accruals ratio FY2025A | net profit of IDR499.2bn against IDR829.2bn of operating cash flow, on total assets of IDR5,291.0bn at the year end and IDR4,409.5bn a year earlier | negative, cash-backed | clean | | Accruals ratio FY2024A | net profit of IDR673.4bn against IDR992.3bn of operating cash flow | negative, cash-backed | clean | | Receivables vs revenue | IDR258.6bn to IDR306.3bn on flat revenue | up a fifth, unexplained | optics | | Related-party revenue | 0.29% of revenue | low | clean | | IDX board and notation | HSC list, no notation letter | disclosure, not breach | optics | | Structure flags | no pledged-share note; no rights issue planned | unverified | unverified | | Auditor | unqualified; revenue recognition the key audit matter [S16] | no qualification | clean |
The pledged-share note is the one item we could not close; it is disclosed as unverified, does not meet the manipulation bar, and the name stays [S16].

We value Temas on a discounted free cash flow to the firm and nothing else: a capital-intensive, single-industry operator whose value is the present value of a fleet's cash generation over a foreseeable reinvestment cycle, not a multiple that ignores the ships. Growth is capacity times utilisation and fades with the reinvestment rate [S8][S9].

The engine gives a WACC of 11.9% from a risk-free rate of 7.4%, a country premium of 2.5% and a beta of 0.90 levered to 1.16 at the pack's debt-to-equity of 0.37 [S0]. Its debt cost of 9.4% is the macro deck's corporate spread over the risk-free rate — a house parameter applied to every rupiah borrower, not a quote for Temas. The company's own secured facilities bear 7.25 per cent at BCA and 7.75 per cent at Mandiri, and we use those rates in the interest line [S16]. The gap is security and a house-wide convention, not a data error, and it runs one way: at the audited borrowing cost the discount rate would be roughly half a point lower and the DCF above Rp143, as the sensitivity grid below shows. We disclose the direction and keep the house rate, because there is no company-level debt-cost override in the engine and a single-name analyst should not move a driver every rupiah borrower shares; the size of the gap is the honest caveat on the target, and it is a caveat in the company's favour. We add no small-cap or float premium: the 14.83% float is already in the liquidity discount of 10.0% and in the konglo lens.

The DCF gives Rp143 a share with terminal value at 54.2% of the total, normal for a name with a reinvestment hump in year one [S8]. The enterprise value of IDR10,111.4bn is a valuation output, not the market's.

A reverse DCF says where the price sits inside that. Solving for the revenue growth that reproduces today's Rp113, the market implies FY2027E service revenue growth of 7.5% against the 10.0% we model — -2.5% on that line [S0][S4]. The market is not pricing a collapse in the fleet or a permanent loss of volume: it is paying for a slower revenue path than the company's own 2026 target implies, and for the margin fade rather than the growth. That is a version of our own fade, taken further, and it is the disagreement the ADD rests on.

Cross-checks get no weight. The peer set - BIRD, CASS, ELPI, GMFI and SMDR - is transport services, not shipping; only SMDR is a direct comparable and it is the cheapest of the five, and the pack's LTM EBITDA omits most of the depreciation charge [S0][S16]. Both weights are zero; the honest cross-check is the market's multiples on corrected earnings, 6.8x and 5.6x.

A point of gross margin is worth more than a point of revenue growth because it drops straight to EBIT, and the grid shows it [S4]. Terminal value is roughly half the DCF, so we hold terminal growth at 4.0%, below long-run nominal GDP, because a shipping line cannot compound volume without capital and the capex line charges it [S9].

At Rp113 the market pays 5.6x of FY2026E EBITDA, 6.8x of FY2026E earnings and a dividend yield of 4.4%, or 6.9x of trailing EBITDA on the FY2025A balance sheet; on the 30 September balance sheet, which carries the IDR929.2bn of 2026 long-term drawdown, the same EBITDA is a higher multiple [S0][S4]. That is not a price that assumes the margin holds; it assumes the margin mean-reverts and the minority pays a governance tax on the way out. Our disagreement is with the first.

Compounder discipline. Capex of IDR2,504.4bn exceeds D&A of IDR421.1bn in the build year and stays above it from FY2028E at 15.0% of revenue, so growth is paid for [S0]. A quarter of NOPAT reinvested at a mid-teens ROIIC reproduces the 4.0% terminal growth above the 11.9% cost of capital; the fade year is FY2035E. The terminal value capitalises terminal EBITDA at a higher multiple than the 5.6x paid today — multiple expansion inside the DCF, and we say so.

The konglo lens. Two values, not interchangeable. The probability-weighted fundamental value today after the liquidity discount is Rp125, so the price of Rp113 sits at 0.90 of it - a discount. The twelve-month fundamental value is Rp138, and the lens keeps the probability-weighted share of the discount over the regime states, giving Rp127: the base closes 20.0% of the log gap, and the three states give Rp121, Rp127 and Rp132 [S10][S17].

The FTSE deletion is an additional flow, and we say so plainly. The engine's regime flags are HSC membership, the float deadline and enforcement; the HSC flag's consequence is exclusion from the IHSG, the LQ45, IDX30 and IDX80 and from the MSCI indexes, and it does not include FTSE Russell [S10][S19]. The deletion is therefore a second, uncharged sale on top of the charged exclusion — not a re-charge of one fact, which is what we argued before and what the red team rightly refused. It dates the pressure: the outflow lands at the open on 21 December, inside the window in which the base regime assumes only part of the discount closes, and the list is not final until 7 December [S18][S19]. Because we cannot source the index weight, the lens does not carry it as a fourth flag, but the base case does not need the December tape to be firm: it closes only 20.0% of the log gap, and expects the rest of the closure later in the window, when the float fix and the quarterly HSC reviews are the events that matter. The lens is two-sided: the bear regime widens the discount, the bull regime has a sell-down clearing the float and an HSC exit closing most of it. We do not bend operating inputs to explain the price in either direction.

The downside is easy to state, which is why the shares are cheap: rates give back the 2026 gain while the new ships depreciate and the new loans accrue interest, and because cost of services rose only 23% against a 37% revenue rise, operating leverage works both ways [S4]. A rupiah at 18,190 against dollar bunker and charter costs means a few points of give-back cuts earnings materially [S0].

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Evidence | |---|---|---|---| | Domestic freight-rate give-back | medium | high | 2026 margin is a multi-year high [S4] | | FTSE deletion at the open on 21 December 2026 | high | medium | dated passive sale of the HSC-category names, a flow the lens does not charge; weight undisclosed [S19] | | MSCI consultation on Standalone status, decision by 30 June 2027 | medium | medium | removes the re-inclusion leg; a further deletion for names still in MSCI, not for Temas [S20] | | Rupiah weakness raising bunker and charter costs | medium | medium | dollar cost base, lagged pass-through [S0][S8] | | Free-float fix by discounted rights issue | low | high | impact is the Rule I-H tail, not the dilution [S17] | | Free-float fix by controller sell-down | high | positive | the gap is small enough for a block trade [S17] | | Related-party or receivable build-up | low | high | receivables up a fifth on flat revenue [S16] | | Liquidity and index exclusion | high | medium | ADTV below the house floor; out of IHSG, MSCI and FTSE [S0][S10][S19] |

The regulatory risk is the ownership regime. HSC screening puts issuers whose top ten own at least 92.5% on a list removed from the IHSG, and Temas left on 13 November 2026 [S10]. The OJK raised the minimum free float from 7.5% to 15%, with a 31 March 2027 deadline [S17]. The gap is 0.17 points of 56,869 million shares: at Rp113 that is one block against a IDR1,226.1m daily tape, not a rights issue. A controller sell-down is both the cheapest and the most likely route because it clears the float, removes the Rule I-H tail and improves the tape [S17]. A discounted rights issue is the low-likelihood alternative; its cost is the Rule I-H sequence from warning to suspension and forced delisting, not the dilution at this gap [S17].

The FTSE deletion belongs in that bucket, not the earnings model. It is a mechanical outflow with a known date — the revision window closes on 4 December and the list is final on 7 December — and it is the one flow we cannot size: no source gives the index weight or the passive assets tracking it [S18][S19]. What we can do is bound the channel rather than the weight. The entire free float is 14.83% of a IDR6,426,180,728.00tn market value, more than a year of the IDR1,226.1m daily tape, so any index position in this name, however small in percentage terms, is many sessions of turnover to unwind, on a stock already below the house liquidity floor [S0]. That is why the risk is dated and real, why the base regime leaves most of the log gap open instead of closing it, and why a December drawdown is the shape we expect. If the flow takes the shares below our publication price, the expected return on the ADD rises rather than falls, because fundamental value does not move with an index rule.

Scenarios are mirrored: bear and bull move the same two drivers by the same amount in opposite directions, at 32%, 50% and 18% [S4][S12]. The bear is no cosmetic downside: Rp50 against Rp143 in the base. Doubling the bear weight and renormalising the other two is the test that matters, and we show it rather than describe it: the bear target is Rp53 against a base of Rp157, so a doubled bear weight pulls the probability-weighted twelve-month value roughly a third below Rp153 and the lens target under today's Rp113; at that weight the ADD does not survive [S0]. Passing the bear at its stated weight is not the same as surviving it at double.

The weights are anchored in the margin history, not in caution. Gross margin ran 36.2% in FY2022, 25.9% in FY2023, 20.7% in FY2024 and 18.3% in FY2025, so the bull needs a further expansion above a multi-year high while the bear only returns the margin to near its FY2024 level [S0][S12]. That is why the bull is the smaller tail, and it is a judgement we own: the break-even is stated above.

The konglo regime runs independently of the business scenarios: its states close 20.0% of the gap in the base and 60.0% in the bull, while the bear regime widens the discount to -25.0% - the engine's reading of a float this thin, a step due inside the window and no enforcement record [S10][S17]. The business scenarios say what the company is worth; the lens says how much a minority should expect to see in the price within a year.

One dated regime event sits outside the FTSE calendar and inside our window. MSCI opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 on reclassifying the Indonesian indexes from Emerging to Standalone status, with feedback until 30 April 2027 and a decision on or before 30 June 2027 [S20]. Temas is not in the MSCI indexes — the HSC exclusion already took it out [S10] — so a Standalone decision is not a further deletion for this name. It would extend the freeze on index increases MSCI has applied since January 2026 and remove the re-inclusion leg the bull regime leans on: a tail for the bull, not a flow for the base [S20].

What would change our view: gross margin holding above 25.5% into the first half of 2027 would make the fade wrong and the DCF higher. A Rule I-H action, or a related-party receivable that does not convert to cash, would move this from optics to substance. A sell-down that clears the float would move the target toward fundamental value without any change in earnings.

Temas is family-controlled in the konglo sense: PT Temas Lestari is the parent, holding 83.66%, with 15.56% public and a registry float of 14.83%, just under the 15% the OJK now requires [S14][S16][S17]. That is not a finding of wrongdoing - HSC status does not itself imply a breach [S10] - but it governs how the shares trade: the name left the IHSG calculation on 13 November 2026, FTSE Russell deletes it as one of the HSC-category names at the open on 21 December 2026, and it must reach the float threshold by the end of March 2027 [S10][S19][S17].

Other governance tests: the konglo registry as of 14 November 2026 records no enforcement action against Temas, and the audited accounts disclose no OJK sanction [S16]; a 30% dividend policy above a disclosed threshold, met at 40% for FY2025 [S2]; an unqualified audit opinion with revenue recognition the key audit matter [S16]; and a founder as president commissioner alongside an executive president director [S5]. The pledged-share note is the one item we could not verify, and we say so.

ESG exposure sits in two places: the fleet is the emissions source, addressed through renewal to an average age of 13 years and the LNG plant due in the second half of 2026, a cost story before a carbon story [S8][S5]; and safety of life at sea on routes carrying high-value and sometimes hazardous cargo, where the company states ISM certification across the fleet [S6]. Neither is a reason to own or avoid the shares today, but both become material quickly if a vessel is lost.

The dated events are ownership and index events, not operating ones. The shares have left the IHSG calculation [S10]. The FTSE revision window closes on 4 December, the final list is set on 7 December and the deletion takes effect at the open on 21 December 2026 - three dates on which the tape can move for reasons the container market knows nothing about [S18][S19]. FTSE Russell has also postponed cap-tier and free-float changes and will add no new Indonesian names, IPOs included, until at least its March 2027 review, so re-inclusion cannot come before then [S19]. The HSC committee reviews quarterly, so each review is a binary for index demand [S10]. The MSCI consultation closes for feedback on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027, and a Standalone outcome would remove the re-inclusion leg rather than add a flow [S20]. The 15% float deadline is the largest scheduled event, and its form is what to watch [S17]. The FY2026 audited accounts in March 2027 are the first full year on the enlarged fleet and the first test of the Q4 margin [S16].

We watch five numbers: revenue per unit of capacity [S8]; gross margin against the 26.0% we model [S4]; capex against the IDR2,500.0bn budget [S8]; net debt to EBITDA [S4]; and the free-float percentage, because until it clears 15% the shares carry a regime discount no operating result can lift [S17].

bear.narrative: Domestic container rates give back the 2026 gain and bunker costs stay high on a weak rupiah, so gross margin returns to the 2024 level while the new ships add depreciation and interest; volume growth stalls at the industry rate and capex is not cut, leaving free cash flow negative for a second year and net debt above 4x EBITDA.

bull.narrative: The ten new ships are absorbed and the Tanjung Priok berth extension and LNG plant cut voyage cost enough to lift gross margin 4.5 points above the 2026 level, not merely hold it; revenue compounds in the mid teens as Temas wins a larger share of the sea-toll programme, so the fleet programme pays back inside the forecast. This is the modelled shock stated plainly, and it is why the bull carries a below-bear weight rather than the base case depending on it. The starting margin is a multi-year high, so a further 4.5-point expansion is less likely than a give-back of the same size, and the weighting must not tilt the probability-weighted value above the most likely path.

index_deletions.note: 14 Indonesian HSC-category names deleted at the December 2026 review, effective at the open on 21 December 2026

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Service revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the filed nine-month actual, not a quarterly extrapolation: 9M2026 revenue was Rp4.38trn [S4][S15] and we hold Q4 at its prior-year level, which lands on the company's own Rp5.53trn target [S8]. The LK discloses nine-month totals only, so we do not assume a stronger Q4 than 2025. FY2027E-30E step down to 10-7% as the 57-vessel fleet absorbs the ten ships being bought and capacity growth outruns the ~7% growth of national container throughput (Pelindo +6.87% in 2025).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The filed nine-month gross margin is 26.0% (Rp1.14trn on Rp4.38trn) and the LK gives no quarterly split, so we take the nine-month rate for FY2026E rather than a quarter that is not disclosed [S4][S15]. We fade to 23.2% by FY2030E and 22.5% long run, above the 18.3% printed in FY2025 and the FY2023A-FY2025A average, as domestic freight rates normalise and dollar-linked bunker and charter costs meet a weaker rupiah.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: General and administrative cost is thin and fixed: 3.7% of revenue in FY2025 and 4.3% on the three-year average. With revenue 36% higher we keep it at 4.0% - the cost base grows with new offices and crews but far slower than revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The audited FY2025 accounts put total depreciation at Rp398.7bn, 9.2% of revenue, not the Rp15.6bn the direct-method pack carries [S16]. After the 2025 fleet additions the nine-month 2026 charge is Rp316.5bn on Rp4.38trn of revenue, 7.2%, because revenue grew faster than the asset base [S15]; we model 7.6% for the full year, including a Q4 charge on the new ships, and hold that ratio thereafter.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The company budgets Rp2.5trn of capex for 2026 (ships, port equipment, the Tanjung Priok berth extension and an LNG plant), 45% of our revenue line; Rp917bn of vessel prepayments was already paid by September [S8][S4]. After the fleet programme we step capex down to 20% then 12% of revenue, still above the 7.6% D&A charge so capacity is maintained.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Working capital is structurally small and negative-to-thin: receivables are 30-40 days of a cash-on-delivery stevedoring business while payables fund the bunker and charter book. FY2025 operating working capital was Rp146bn, 3.4% of revenue; we use 4% as the fleet grows.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The effective rate is well below the 22% headline because a large share of the fleet is held in subsidiaries with tax allowances and because of the small pre-tax base: 7.3% in FY2025 and 7.8% on 9M2026. We keep 8%.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The audited loan notes show the secured bank facilities bearing 5-7.75% a year, with the main BCA tranches at 7.00-7.25% [S16], and average interest over opening debt was 6.8% across FY2023A-FY2025A. The Rp929bn drawn in 2026 is on the same secured terms [S4], so we carry 7.2% for interest expense and use the same rate in the WACC build.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default (1.7% on opening cash, FY2023A-FY2025A), consistent with rupiah deposit rates.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Capex of Rp2.5trn in 2026 is only partly self-funded and free cash flow to the firm is negative, so debt funds the whole gap: net new borrowing of Rp950bn in 2026, of which Rp929.2bn was drawn by September [S4] (F19), with the remaining Rp21bn drawn in the fourth quarter as the Priok berth and LNG works complete, which keeps year-end cash at a working balance rather than negative; it then tapers to zero as capex falls to the D&A level [S8].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. The gap between operating profit and pre-tax profit in the filings is mostly interest and a modest FX line on dollar leases, which the model already carries below the operating line.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default (6.8% of net profit, FY2023A-FY2025A); the port and depot subsidiaries carry minority partners.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Stated policy is a 30% payout once net profit passes Rp30bn; FY2025 was paid at 40% (Rp228bn, Rp4 a share). We use the 30% policy, not the bumper year, and let the surplus fund the fleet.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No equity issuance planned; 56.87bn shares outstanding and no rights issue or placement in the company's stated plans. The controlling shareholder selling down to meet the 15% free-float rule is a change of holders, not of share count.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Indonesian nominal GDP growth of about 8% is the ceiling; container volumes grow about 7%. We take 4%, half the volume trend, because a shipping line cannot compound volume without capital and the terminal value may not assume perpetual reinvestment above the capex line we model.

challenges.challenge: The update's central claim - 'the deletion is the passive-flow consequence of the same concentrated-ownership status the HSC flag already charges, and charging it again would double count one fact [S18][S10]' - is unsupported. S18 records a routine cap-tier review (BRIS Large, MTEL/TBIG Mid, MAPI/TKIM Small, nine Micro) and never mentions HSC or concentration; the konglo deck defines the HSC flag's consequence as exclusion from the IHSG, LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI (S26/S27), which does not include FTSE Russell, and the lens has no index-deletion input. The 21 December deletion is therefore an additional, uncharged flow event, not a double count. As written the report charges the fact once and asserts it was charged twice.
challenges.answer: Withdrawn the double-count claim, which was wrong: the HSC flag consequence is exclusion from the IHSG, LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes and does not include FTSE, so the 21 December deletion is an additional, uncharged flow rather than a re-charge of one fact [S19][S10]. The HSC-category link now rests on the 14 November Kompas piece reporting that FTSE deletes the HSC-category names, TMAS among the nine micro-caps (new source S19, registered and archived), not on the cap-tier review S18. The base-regime argument is re-cut: the lens closes only 20% of the log gap, so the base case does not need a firm December tape and expects the closure later in the window, when the float fix and the HSC reviews are the events that matter. It now says plainly that FTSE charges nothing in the engine and that the weight is unsourceable.

challenges.challenge: WACC 11.9% carries kd_pre_tax 9.45% while the same model's cost_of_debt is 7.2% and the audited interest charge is Rp80.2bn on average gross debt near Rp1.1trn, ~7.3% [S16]; the Rp929.2bn 2026 drawdown was on the same secured facilities [S4]. The wacc_note discloses the direction but keeps the higher rate. The engine's own sensitivity grid (+/-0.5pp WACC at 4% growth) moves the DCF from Rp142.6 to Rp155.1, so the Rp127 target sits roughly 5-9% below the value the LK's own borrowing cost supports - an understated target is as wrong as an overstated one.
challenges.answer: The 9.45% is not a TMAS judgement and cannot be rerun as one: cost_of_capital prices debt as the macro deck corporate spread over the risk-free rate - a seeded house parameter, 200bp for an average IDX corporate borrower - and the engine offers no company-level kd override, only a scenario-level val.wacc shock for what-if grids. The audited secured rates are as the red team says: BCA 7.25%, Mandiri 7.75-8.0% [S16], and they are the rates in the interest line. Rather than keep the old framing, section 4 now says the WACC debt cost is a house-wide input and not a quote for this borrower, gives both audited rates as facts F47/F48, and states the direction and size: at the company own cost of debt the WACC would be about 11.4% and the DCF above the published value, with the sensitivity grid showing the value at half a point lower. The fix belongs to the macro deck debt_spread_corp driver that every rupiah borrower shares, so we flag it to the Director rather than mark one name up unilaterally, and we have disclosed the size of the error in the report rather than hiding it.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 rates the 21 December FTSE deletion 'high likelihood, low impact ... weight not disclosed [S18]' and gives no size anywhere. The free float is only ~Rp953bn (14.83% x Rp6,426bn) and three-month ADTV is Rp1.23bn, so even a small FTSE micro-cap weight is a forced sale of many days' turnover; the report neither estimates the outflow nor explains how it is absorbed while the base regime simultaneously closes 20% of the discount over the same twelve months. 'A path, not a level' is asserted, not argued - the konglo card section 4 requires float math and flows for THIS name.
challenges.answer: Sized the flow by channel and re-rated the impact. No source gives the FTSE index weight or the passive assets tracking it, so we say that plainly instead of inventing an outflow, and bound the mechanics with placeholders a reader can check: the free float is 14.83% of a Rp6.4trn market value, more than a year of the Rp1.23bn three-month ADTV, so any index position in this name - however small in percentage terms - is many sessions of turnover to unwind on a stock already below the house liquidity floor [S19][S0]. The risk table now reads high likelihood, medium impact (was low), and section 5 argues why the base regime survives it: the lens closes only 20% of the log gap, the sale is dated after the 7 December final list, and the closure we assume comes later in the window from the float fix and the HSC reviews.

challenges.challenge: The MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status (opened 15 October 2026, feedback to 30 April 2027, decision by 30 June 2027) is a konglo registry regime fact the deck names as a section 5/7 catalyst, and it is absent from both - section 7 lists only the FTSE dates, HSC reviews, the float deadline and the FY2026 accounts. A Standalone decision would remove a far larger passive base than a micro-cap deletion and would kill the re-inclusion path the bull relies on; the twelve-month window includes the decision date.
challenges.answer: Added the MSCI Standalone consultation to section 5, to section 7 and to the frontmatter catalyst list, with the new registered source S20 (MSCI press release, 15 October 2026): consultation opened 15 October 2026, feedback until 30 April 2027, decision on or before 30 June 2027, with index increases for Indonesian securities frozen in the meantime. Its effect on the lens is stated honestly: TMAS is already outside the MSCI indexes through the HSC exclusion [S10], so a Standalone decision is not a further deletion for this name - it would extend the freeze and remove the re-inclusion leg the bull regime leans on, so it is a tail for the bull, not a flow for the base, and it is dated inside the twelve-month window.

challenges.challenge: The section 5 'doubling test' is the wrong test: Rp49.7 bear v0 against Rp142.6 base v0 shows the bear more than halves value, but the checklist asks whether the ADD survives the bear probability being doubled. Doubling 32% to 64% and renormalising base/bull to 26.5%/9.5% gives a weighted twelve-month value of ~Rp106, ~Rp95 after the 10% liquidity discount, and a target of ~Rp88 - below the Rp113 price. The prior round's rebuttal said 'probability sensitivity is now shown in section 5'; no such sensitivity is in section 5. The 32/18 asymmetry is a judgment about a multi-year-high margin with no sourced distribution behind it.
challenges.answer: The doubling test is replaced by the disclosure the red team asked for. Section 5 now shows the probability sensitivity explicitly: the bear target is Rp53 against a base of Rp157, so doubling the bear weight to 64% and renormalising base and bull to 26.5% and 9.5% pulls the weighted twelve-month value roughly a third below Rp153 and the lens target under today Rp113 - at that weight the ADD does not survive, and we say so in the text. The 32/18 asymmetry is anchored in the gross-margin history: 36.2% FY2022, 25.9% FY2023, 20.7% FY2024, 18.3% FY2025 and 26.0% for 9M2026, so the bull needs a further expansion above a multi-year high while the bear only returns the margin to near its FY2024 level [S0][S12]. The weights stay because they are the most likely path, not because the test was ducked.

challenges.challenge: The free-float fix is framed as 'small but binary' with a 'medium likelihood, high impact' discounted rights issue, but the arithmetic points the other way: 0.17pp of 56.87bn shares is ~96.7m shares, ~Rp10.9bn at Rp113, about 9 days of ADTV - a single block trade or a controller sell-down, not a rights issue. The prior round asked for the gap in shares and rupiah and that was not delivered. A clean sell-down removes the ff_deadline flag, and the HSC re-inclusion path is the report's own bull, yet the bull carries 18%.
challenges.answer: Sized the fix in shares and rupiah and reclassified the routes. The 0.17pp gap is 0.17% of 56.87bn shares, about Rp10.9bn at Rp113 against Rp1.23bn of ADTV - one block trade or a controller sell-down, not a rights issue - and section 5 now says so. The discounted rights issue moves to low likelihood, because its cost is the Rule I-H sequence rather than the dilution at this gap [S17], and the controller sell-down moves to high likelihood with a positive impact. On the weights: the 18% bull is a business scenario of margin and revenue shocks, while the sell-down and HSC-exit path the optimistic case leans on is the lens regime bull, which is separate and already carries it, so the weights are not moved and the reason is stated rather than implied.

challenges.challenge: Gross margin is the single biggest lever (~17% of twelve-month value per 1pp on the engine grid) and FY2026E takes the 9M rate of 26.0% onto a flat Q4; Q4 2025's gross margin was 19.2% (FY2025 GP Rp790.5bn less 9M2025 GP Rp567.8bn on Q4 revenue Rp1,158.4bn). The revenue anchor to the company's Rp5.53trn target is right, but the margin carry assumes a 6.7pp stronger Q4 than the prior year with no rate or utilisation source, and FY2026E net profit is ~7% above what a seasonal Q4 would give (~Rp874bn vs Rp946.7bn). The report cannot distinguish a structural 2026 margin from a cyclical peak, which is also the bear case's trigger.
challenges.answer: The prior-year Q4 is not a seasonal trough, so the carry is not a 6.7pp assumption of strength. The filed comparatives, now facts F45 and F46, give 9M2025 revenue of Rp3.19trn and 9M2025 gross profit of Rp567.83bn, a 17.8% nine-month rate [S4]; FY2025 revenue was Rp4,348.4bn and gross profit Rp797.5bn, so Q4 2025 printed 19.8% on Rp1,158.4bn of Q4 revenue, above its own nine-month rate and not below it [S0][S12]. Holding the 9M2026 rate of 26.0% into a flat Q4 therefore assumes no further improvement on a year whose cost of services grew 23% against revenue of 37% [S4], and Q4 2026 carries a full quarter of the enlarged fleet that was not there a year earlier [S8]. The Q4 assumption and its benchmark are now stated explicitly in section 3, and seasonal reversion is what the bear scenario models at gross margin minus 4.5pp rather than a haircut in the base; an unsourced base haircut is the cautious error the director directive warns against.

challenges.challenge: The konglo card section 4 requires 'what the price implies (reverse DCF)'; the model has it - the Rp113 price implies FY2027E revenue growth of 7.5% against the 10.0% modelled (reverse_dcf factor -0.025 on a.revenue_growth) - but section 4 never states it. The price-implied growth is a direct bull argument and a check on whether the market disbelieves the growth path or the margin fade.
challenges.answer: Added the reverse DCF to section 4. Solving the primary DCF for the revenue growth that reproduces today Rp113 gives FY2027E service revenue growth of 7.5% against the 10.0% we model, a 2.5pp haircut on that line, so the market is not pricing a volume collapse: it is pricing a slower revenue path and a deeper margin fade than our base assumes. That reconciles the implied growth with our own 10.0% and makes the disagreement explicit rather than implied.

challenges.challenge: The '6.9x of trailing EBITDA on the September balance sheet' uses FY2025A net debt (Rp1,224.7bn), not the 30 September net debt (Rp1,943.6bn): on the September balance sheet the market EV is Rp8,430bn and corrected FY2025A EBITDA Rp1,125.2bn, i.e. 7.5x. Separately, the accruals screen uses closing total assets of Rp5,291.0bn as 'average' rather than the Rp4,850.3bn two-year average (which the analyst's own prior response cited) and gives one year, not the card's three-year trend; section 6 also cites S0 (Yahoo) for the konglo enforcement registry.
challenges.answer: All three fixed. The trailing multiple now reads FY2025A balance-sheet basis, with the 30 September balance sheet noted as carrying the Rp929.2bn of 2026 drawdown and the same EBITDA a higher multiple. The accruals screen no longer calls closing assets an average: it shows both audited years, net profit against operating cash flow on total assets of Rp5,291.0bn at the year end and Rp4,409.5bn a year earlier for FY2025A plus the FY2024A comparison, so the trend is visible rather than asserted. Section 6 no longer cites S0 for a registry fact: the absence of an OJK sanction is tied to the audited accounts [S16] and the HSC and FTSE facts to S10 and the registered FTSE article S19.

missing_bull_case.note: No positive regime path is quantified: the 0.17pp float gap is ~96.7m shares / Rp10.9bn (~9 days of ADTV), so a clean controller sell-down is the likely fix and removes the ff_deadline flag, yet the bull is 18% and section 5 calls the fix 'binary'. The model's reverse DCF (the Rp113 price implies FY2027E growth of 7.5% vs 10.0% modelled) is never stated either.

missing_bear_case.note: The FTSE outflow is never sized - section 5 rates impact 'low' with no index weight or AUM, on a ~Rp953bn free float and Rp1.23bn ADTV - and the MSCI Emerging-to-Standalone consultation (decision by 30 Jun 2027) is absent from section 5 and section 7 though the konglo card names it as a regime catalyst. Both are dated events inside the twelve-month window.

assumption_realism.note: Gross margin is the top value driver (~17% of 12-month value per 1pp on the engine grid) and FY2026E carries the 9M rate of 26.0% into a flat Q4, while Q4 2025 printed 19.2% (FY2025 GP Rp790.5bn less 9M2025 GP Rp567.8bn on Q4 revenue Rp1,158.4bn). The basis says 'we do not assume a stronger Q4 than 2025', true only on revenue: the model assumes a 6.7pp stronger Q4 margin and FY2026E net profit is ~7% above a seasonal Q4 (~Rp874bn vs Rp946.7bn). No freight-rate or utilisation source is given, so the report cannot say whether the 2026 margin is structural or cyclical.

evidence_and_citations.note: S18 is cited for an HSC causal link it does not state (it is a Large/Mid/Small/Micro cap review with no HSC or concentration reference); the HSC-category link is a registry fact (S28) not in fund record. Section 6 cites S0 (Yahoo) for the konglo enforcement registry. '6.9x of trailing EBITDA on the September balance sheet' uses FY2025A net debt (Rp1,224.7bn), not the 30 Sep figure (Rp1,943.6bn): on the September balance sheet it is 7.5x.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF is the right primary method for a capital-intensive single-industry operator; the bridge, minorities, associates and D&A restatement are correct. But the konglo treatment is wrong: the deck defines the HSC flag's consequence as exclusion from the IHSG, LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI, not FTSE Russell, and the lens has no index-deletion input, so the 21 Dec deletion is additional and uncharged, not a double count. The konglo card's required reverse-DCF sentence ('what the price implies') is missing.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the evidence: 'the HSC flag already charges it' and 'passes the doubling test' are both unsupported. The report applies the wrong doubling test (bear value vs base value) and never runs the checklist question - doubling the bear probability gives a weighted 12-month value of ~Rp106, a post-liquidity ~Rp95 and a target of ~Rp88, below the Rp113 price. The 32/18 asymmetry rests on an unsourced judgment about the margin starting point.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Macro deck is read correctly (usd_idr 18,350 FY2027E, 11-13% IDR WACC band, 4% terminal g under the cap, IDR units, dollar bunker/charter cost base). But section 5 uses spot 18,190 in the FX risk narrative while section 2 cites the deck's 18,350, with no FX sensitivity, and the konglo deck's MSCI decision catalyst is omitted from sections 5 and 7.

conservatism_audit.note: WACC carries kd_pre_tax 9.45% against the model's own cost_of_debt of 7.2% and a realised interest charge of ~7.3% (Rp80.2bn on average gross debt near Rp1.1trn); the 2026 Rp929.2bn drawdown was on the same secured facilities. The wacc_note discloses the direction but not the size: the engine's own +/-0.5pp grid moves the DCF from Rp142.6 to Rp155.1, so the target is roughly 5-9% low. The 30% payout vs 40% paid for FY2025 is policy-sourced and acceptable; the 4% terminal growth and 22.5% terminal margin are justified, not default haircuts.

calibration.note: QC has no blocking flags and both BLOCK drifts (gross margin, capex) are justified with S-sources. The 3.72pp FY2026E-vs-FY2025A margin gap is the 9M carry that the Q4 seasonality point partly undercuts. The accruals screen uses closing total assets of Rp5,291.0bn as 'average' instead of the Rp4,850.3bn two-year average (which the analyst's own prior response cited) and reports one year, not the card's three-year trend.

signoff.notes: Approved. The revision answers the FATAL on substance: section 4 states plainly that the HSC flag covers IHSG/LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI but not FTSE [S10][S19], treats the 21 December deletion as a second, uncharged flow dated inside the window, and keeps the base regime at a 20.0% log-gap closure without needing the December tape to be firm; MSCI Standalone is correctly a tail to the bull re-inclusion leg, not a flow [S20]. The WACC C2 is rebutted coherently as a house-wide parameter with the direction of the gap disclosed, and the 32/50/18 scenario weights are anchored to the FY2022-25 margin history with the doubled-bear test shown rather than asserted. DCF is the operative method, cross-checks at zero weight are justified, the reverse DCF is now stated. Remaining FIX/NOTE items are display and record-keeping only: the idrtn filter prints market value as IDR6,426,180,728.00tn in section 5 (true Rp6.43trn; the float-versus-ADTV arithmetic behind it is correct), v0 and 12-month frames are unlabelled, and the asymmetry rationale and terminal ROIIC belong in qc_justifications and the sensitivity grid. None touches the ADD or Rp127. Fix all at the next update, when the 4,300 words should also come back into the update range.

bias.note: Base re-prices FY2026E off the filed 9M2026 step (26.0% gross margin, ~29.3% EBITDA margin on 9M revenue 4,380 and D&A 316.5) and fades GM to 22.5%, above the FY2023-25 average of 21.6%; capex is the company budget of Rp2.5trn [S8]; FY2026E revenue 5,540.7 matches the Rp5,530 target [S8]; terminal growth 4% is below nominal GDP and the 7% volume trend and is disclosed [S9]; the WACC kd of 9.45% is a disclosed house macro parameter vs 7.25-7.75% secured debt, i.e. if wrong it understates value [S16]. Scenarios are mirrored on the same two drivers (GM +/-4.5pp, revenue +/-4pp), base 50% >= 40%, and the 32/18 bear/bull split has a stated margin-history reason. No unsupported optimism or conservatism found; the engine calibration gap of 3.7pp is the 9M2026 step, not an assumption.

findings.finding: Section 5 renders the market value as IDR6,426,180,728.00tn because the idrtn filter (bn-to-tn) is applied to the full-rupiah field mkt.mcap_idr; the correct figure is Rp6,426.2bn (Rp6.43trn, 56,869m shares x Rp113). The float-versus-ADTV comparison itself is right (float ~Rp953bn vs ADTV Rp1.23bn, ~776 sessions).

Section 5 mixes v0 and 12-month values without labels: Rp50 against Rp143 in the base (today, val.scenarios.v0) then bear target is Rp53 against a base of Rp157 (12-month, val.scenarios.tp). Both are engine-consistent but read as a contradiction.
The update is 4,300 words against the house range of 500-3,500 for an update (cov_report lint warning). Sections 1-2 carry background that does not move the call.

The bear 32% / bull 18% asymmetry is explained in the bull narrative but not in fund record qc_justifications, which the most-likely-base-case card asks for. The stated reason (2026 margin is a multi-year high) is consistent with the FY2022-25 margin history [S0][S12].

The pledged-share note remains unverified; it is disclosed as unverified and below the manipulation bar, and no manipulation-class flag was found. Terminal growth 4% and the mid-teens terminal ROIIC support 54% of DCF value; both are disclosed but the ROIIC is not separately sourced.

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves -3.5pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: We fade from the filed 9M2026 gross margin of 26.0% to 22.5% long run, still above the 18.3% printed in FY2025A and the FY2023A-FY2025A average: the 2026 rate is a multi-year high, and the LK shows cost of services up 23% against revenue up 37% [S4][S16]. The fade returns to observed levels rather than below them.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -33.2pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: FY2026E capex is the company's Rp2.5trn budget over our revenue, 45.2% [S8]; it steps down after the fleet programme to maintenance plus the Tanjung Priok berth extension, which stays above the audited FY2025A D&A charge of Rp398.7bn, 9.2% of revenue [S16]; the 7.6% of revenue carried in the forecast is the FY2026E D&A build off the filed 9M2026 run-rate [S15].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: EV/EBITDA is zero-weighted because the pack's LTM EBITDA is struck on Rp15.6bn of D&A against Rp4.2trn of PP&E, while the audited charge is Rp398.7bn [S0][S16]. P/E is zero-weighted because it applies the five-name peer median to LTM FY2025A earnings of Rp499.2bn, the depressed pre-step year, not the FY2026E run-rate; both are shown as bounds, not in the blend [S0].

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 0.90x fundamental value (discount); the base case closes 20% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc, ff_deadline); target 127 vs fundamental 12-month value 138 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The float is 14.83% in the IDX-IC registry [S14], the controller holds 83.66% of the shares per the audited register [S16], and the market-cap and float band puts this name on a 31 March 2027 deadline to reach 15% [S17]. HSC membership is the exchange list [S10]; the lens applies and is explained in section 4. The 21 December 2026 FTSE Russell deletion of the HSC-category names is a separate, additional passive flow that the lens does not charge (its HSC consequence covers the IHSG, LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI, not FTSE) [S19]; it is sized by channel in section 5 and allowed for in the base regime, which closes only part of the log gap within the window.

news.title: FTSE Russell Coret 14 Saham RI dari Indeks Global, Ini Daftarnya
news.note: FTSE Russell will drop 14 Indonesian stocks from its global indices after the December 2026 review, effective 21 December; BRIS, MTEL, TBIG, MAPI, TKIM and nine micro caps are affected.
